name: org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin
description: GW Maven Plugin is a Maven plugin for Machai Ghostwriter guided document processing and documentation automation in Java projects. It scans project documentation trees for embedded guidance tags, applies AI-powered guided transformations, supports interactive action prompts, processes Maven reactor modules either as an aggregator or per-module goal, resolves GenAI credentials from Maven settings, provides classpath introspection tools for Java classes, and cleans temporary Ghostwriter workflow artifacts. The artifact is useful for Java documentation automation, AI-assisted documentation synthesis, Maven build integration, multi-module project processing, and guided file processing workflows.

usageContext: Classpath and Java class metadata introspection
integrations: GenAI provider configured through Maven settings

constructors.description: Creates classpath introspection tools backed by the supplied Maven project. The object scans project output directories and compile classpath entries so tool invocations can find Java classes and inspect reflective metadata relative to the Maven project.

examples.snippet:
org.apache.maven.project.MavenProject project = new org.apache.maven.project.MavenProject();
org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools tools = new org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools(project);
examples.description: Creates a fully qualified ClassFunctionalTools instance for a MavenProject so Java class discovery and metadata lookup can be used by a processing workflow. In normal plugin execution the Maven runtime provides the MavenProject instance.

constructors.description: Creates an empty class introspection tool set. Maven projects must be registered later with scanProjectClasses before class lookup operations can resolve metadata.

examples.description: Creates the tool set first and registers a Maven project later. This is useful when tools are initialized before the current project context is available.

constructors.description: Creates a holder for class discovery and lookup data for a Maven project. It builds a URLClassLoader from compile classpath entries plus main and test output directories, scans visible public and protected classes, and records source paths, class paths, and dependency artifact coordinates.

examples.description: Creates a class metadata holder and loads a fully qualified Java class from the Maven project classpath. The class name inside the snippet is escaped for valid JSON and should be replaced with a project class name.

features.name: gw:gw
features.description: Runs the Ghostwriter guided file processing workflow as an aggregator Maven goal. It can run without a pom.xml, scans documents, processes modules in reverse order so submodules are handled before parent modules, and supports optional multi-threaded module processing through the gw.threads parameter.

examples.description: Installs or resolves the Maven plugin from configured Maven repositories, configures it with gw.path to scan src/site, disables multi-threaded processing, and invokes the gw goal to process guided documentation files in a real Maven project.

features.name: gw:gw-per-module
features.description: Processes documents for the current Maven module as part of the standard Maven reactor. Maven determines module execution order using its dependency graph. The goal initializes a GuidanceProcessor rooted at the reactor execution directory and binds Maven-specific project layout metadata for each module.

examples.description: Runs the per-module goal in a Maven reactor. The example configures the scan directory, points to additional guidance instructions, excludes generated and dependency directories, and lets Maven execute the goal for each active module.

features.name: gw:act
features.description: Runs an interactive or predefined action prompt over scanned documentation. If gw.act is not supplied, the goal prompts the user interactively through Maven Prompter. It supports an optional gw.acts directory containing predefined action definitions and inherited common parameters such as gw.model, gw.path, gw.excludes, genai.serverId, and logInputs.

examples.description: Invokes a ready-to-use Maven plugin goal that applies the configured action text to documentation under src/site. The command enables input logging so users can verify which files were sent to the workflow.

features.name: gw:act-per-module
features.description: Runs an action against the execution-root project using Maven reactor context. It is the non-aggregator, reactor-friendly variant of gw:act and delegates scanning to ActProcessor while inheriting ActMojo and AbstractGWMojo configuration parameters.

examples.description: Runs the action goal in a reactor-friendly mode. Use it when a standard Maven reactor build should apply the same documentation action to module documentation.

features.name: gw:clean
features.description: Deletes temporary artifacts created by Machai Ghostwriter document processing under the current module base directory. This goal is typically bound to Maven's clean phase.

examples.description: Invokes the plugin clean goal to remove workflow temporary files from the current Maven module. It can also be configured in the Maven clean lifecycle for routine cleanup.

features.name: findClass
features.description: Finds fully qualified Java class names whose simple names match the supplied regular expression in the class metadata associated with the given Maven project directory.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools tools = new org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools(project);
java.lang.String matches = tools.findClass(".*Service", new java.io.File("."));
examples.description: Searches for classes whose simple names end with Service in the current project. This is useful for AI-guided documentation workflows that need to reference project classes by fully qualified name.

features.name: getClassInfo
features.description: Returns reflective metadata for a specified Java class, including modifiers, superclass, interfaces, non-private fields, constructors, non-private methods, annotations, class path, and dependency artifact coordinates when available.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools tools = new org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools(project);
java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object> info = tools.getClassInfo("org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.GWMojo", new java.io.File("."));
examples.description: Retrieves structured metadata for the GWMojo class so documentation generation can include constructor, method, annotation, and artifact-origin information.

customizations.name: gw.model
customizations.description: Provider and model identifier forwarded to the workflow, for example CodeMie:gpt-5.5-2026-04-24 or another configured GenAI model.

examples.description: Configures which GenAI model the Ghostwriter workflow should use during guided document processing.

customizations.name: gw.path
customizations.description: Optional scan root override. When omitted, goals use the execution root or current module directory depending on the selected goal.

examples.description: Restricts processing to documentation files below src/site.

customizations.name: genai.serverId
customizations.description: Maven settings.xml server id used to resolve GenAI credentials. When configured, username, password, and custom XML configuration values from the matching server entry are copied to the downstream workflow configuration.

examples.description: Reads GenAI credentials from the Maven settings server with id my-model-server and passes them to the workflow.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.AbstractGWMojo
studs.description: Base class for GWMojo Maven plugin goals. It centralizes shared configuration parameters, resolves optional GenAI credentials from Maven settings.xml, configures document scanning, applies excludes and instructions, registers class-related helper tools, and delegates scanning to the configured processor.

examples.description: Shows how a custom Maven mojo can extend the abstract base class and reuse shared configuration and scanning behavior. Fully qualified names are used for external types.

examples.title: Install and run the GW Maven Plugin with a direct Maven invocation
steps: Ensure Java 8 or newer and Apache Maven 3.8.1 or newer are installed.
Configure access to the repository that contains org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin:1.2.2-SNAPSHOT if the snapshot is not already available locally.
Place guided documentation files under src/site or another documentation directory.
Review the transformed documentation files and generated workflow output.
examples.description: This scenario demonstrates how to resolve and execute the ready-to-use Maven plugin without adding it to pom.xml. It is useful for one-off guided documentation processing.

examples.title: Configure the plugin in pom.xml and process documentation
examples.description: Add the plugin to the build configuration, configure the model, scan path, instructions, and input logging, then invoke the gw goal to run guided document processing.

examples.title: Use an action prompt to rewrite documentation headings
examples.description: This practical action scenario runs the act goal with an explicit prompt. The plugin scans files under src/site, applies the action text to the scanned documentation, and logs selected input files for traceability.

examples.title: Run processing across a multi-module Maven reactor
examples.description: This scenario demonstrates per-module operation. Maven executes the goal in reactor order, the plugin processes each module documentation directory, and generated or dependency folders are excluded.
